Container.Name: isputnik-games
Container.Overview:
Family games for isputnik.home, in a container of their own. Board games: Dots, Star Battle, Chess, Dominoes and Checkers (Russian draughts), played two on one screen, against the computer, or online between family members, who invite each other and play from any device, phone included. Arcade games: Sputnik Catch and Torpedo Run, with a family high-score table. Everything runs on your server; nothing is sent anywhere.
This is an add-on for isputnik.home and does nothing on its own: it has no sign-in and no pages of its own. Install it beside the isputnik container; the family signs in once, in isputnik.home, and finds Games in its menu, at /games on the same address. Set it up from isputnik.home, on Control panel, Settings, Apps, Games. Before installing, press Generate secret there and copy it (it is shown once); paste it into the Gateway Secret field below, which is required. Once the container runs, enter its address on the same page (http://[your Unraid IP]:4200 as installed here) and press Test connection, which then says Paired. Who may play, and from where (home network only, or anywhere), is chosen on Security, App access. Needs isputnik.home 4.38 or newer.
Container.Changes:
### 2026.11.09 — 0.25.2 Named as an add-on, with a change log for Unraid - **Every public description now says what this is: an add-on for isputnik.home.** The GitHub repository, the image on ghcr.io, the Unraid Community Applications template and its profile all say the container is installed beside the isputnik container and reached only through it, so nobody installs it expecting a game server of its own. - **The Unraid template carries its change log.** Community Applications shows when the container was last updated and what changed, from a `Date` and `Changes` block in `isputnik-games.xml` that `npm run changelog` regenerates from `changelog.json` on every release, as isputnik.home's does.
### 2026.11.09 — 0.25.1 Unraid Community Applications listing - **Ready for Unraid Community Applications as isputnik-games.** The template now publishes port 4200 on the ordinary bridge network, so isputnik.home reaches the games at the server's own address with nothing to create first; a shared Docker network or br0 with a fixed IP work as before. It names the games as they stand and sends the administrator to isputnik.home's Control panel → Settings → Apps for the pairing, where the secret is generated first and pasted into the one setting this container has, Gateway Secret. - **The 0.25.0 image was never published.** Its build failed on a type error in a web test, and the image registry kept 0.24.1 as the latest for three days. This release carries everything 0.25.0 announced.
### 2026.11.05 — 0.25.0 The home app's frame on phones - **The games wear the home app's frame.** Stories and Tags join the top bar, phones get home's four tabs and sheets with no top bar, and installing the games page as an app installs iSputnik itself.
### 2026.11.05 — 0.24.1 Clearer Torpedo Run aiming and balanced encounters - **Torpedo Run aims more clearly.** The trajectory is drawn as you aim, the horizon is split into distance bands, ships announce their arrival with a countdown, and encounters are balanced so a run is neither a walkover nor a wall.
### 2026.11.04 — 0.24.0 The games on the TV - **Chess, Checkers, Sputnik Catch and Torpedo Run play on the TV** with a remote, in the iSputnik TV app 0.8. This server answers the TV's positions: a stateless play endpoint for a game against the computer or two on the sofa, and the legal moves of an online match. Nothing changes in the browser.
Container.Requires: Needs the isputnik (isputnik.home) container, version 4.38 or newer, installed on the same server. The games are reached only through it.

Config.Name: Games Port
Config.Description: The port the isputnik container reaches the games on: enter http://[your Unraid IP]:[this port] as the Games address in isputnik.home (Control panel, Settings, Apps). Not for browsers: the games open inside isputnik.home. On br0 with a fixed IP, or on a user-defined network shared with the isputnik container, this mapping is not used and the address is the container's own IP or name with port 4200.

Config.Name: Config & Data
Config.Description: Stores the online matches, scores and the games' own log of events (a small SQLite database). Keep it apart from the isputnik container's appdata. isputnik.home's backups include a copy of it.

Config.Name: Gateway Secret
Config.Description: The secret isputnik.home signs its requests with, so this server knows who is signed in. Make it first, in isputnik.home on Control panel, Settings, Apps, Games (Generate secret; it is shown once), and paste it here. Required: the server refuses to start without one, or with one shorter than 32 characters. Nothing else is set on this container; everything about the games is managed inside isputnik.home.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID the server runs as. It runs unprivileged (not root); on first start it takes ownership of the Config & Data path as this user. 99 (nobody) matches the default owner of an Unraid appdata share - leave it unless your share is owned by a different user.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID the server runs as. 100 (users) matches the default group of an Unraid appdata share - leave it unless your share uses a different group.

Config.Name: Log Level
Config.Description: trace, debug, info, warn, error, fatal or silent. At info every request is logged, including each poll for the other side's move; warn keeps only problems. isputnik.home shows this log and the games' own event record under Control panel, Overview, Logs.
